cards.prose: *Have ye not read what David did*, he asks, and the reading starts here. David comes to Nob, the priest is afraid at the sight of him, and the only bread to be had is the bread set apart for the priests. Nothing in the story calls it a sin, so Yahusha (Jesus) is not loosening the rule about the holy bread, he is reading it the way it was written.
cards.member_phrase: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest
cards.member_sentence: David came to the priest at Nob in need and was given the hallowed bread, and the Scripture tells it without a word of blame.

cards.prose: The Torah itself gives the priests a task for every sabbath, and the verse says so plainly: *Every sabbath he shall set it in order*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says the priests in the temple *profane the sabbath, and are blameless*, he is not pointing at a loophole. He is pointing at work the commandment itself calls for, and it is the very bread David ate.
cards.member_sentence: The bread was set in order before Yahuah (the LORD) every sabbath by an everlasting covenant, so sabbath work was commanded in the Torah itself.

cards.prose: The one who is *Adonai (Lord) even of the sabbath day* is claiming a day, not cancelling one, and Genesis shows whose day it was. Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day and made it holy at the very start, before there was a Pharisee or a fence or a priest, so the Son of Adam is master of a day that was holy before any man laid a rule on it.
cards.member_phrase: blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) blessed the seventh day and made it holy at creation, so the day Yahusha (Jesus) is master of was set apart before any man's rule.

cards.prose: This is the commandment he stands as master over, and nothing he says to the Pharisees sets it down. He is clearing off what men stacked on top of it so that *to keep it holy* can be heard plainly again, and he does it as the one whose voice spoke it in the first place.
cards.member_sentence: The commandment itself, the plain word to remember the sabbath day and keep it holy, which Yahusha (Jesus) stands behind and never sets down.

cards.prose: They ask in the synagogue whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath, and later in John he answers from their own practice. They circumcise a man on the sabbath so the law of Moses will not be broken, and then they are angry that he *made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day* (John 7:23). If one commandment can be kept on the day of the other, healing is no breach.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) answers the sabbath accusation from their own practice: a man is circumcised on the sabbath so the law of Moses is kept, and so a man may be made whole.

cards.prose: He closes the matter with *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days*, and Isaiah shows that is no softening of the day. The prophet calls the sabbath a delight, set apart from doing our own ways, and lifting a man out of his trouble is that delight itself rather than a breach of the day.
cards.member_phrase: call the sabbath a delight, the holy of Yahuah (LORD), honourable
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah calls the sabbath a delight and holy to Yahuah (the LORD), the day on which doing well belongs and the Pharisees' fence does not.

cards.prose: The disciples walk through the field on the sabbath day with their master, and Hebrews shows the day did not stop there. A rest still *remaineth* for the people of Elohim (God), and the next verse says what that rest is: whoever has entered it has *ceased from his own works, as Elohim (God) did from his* (Hebrews 4:10). That is the seventh day's rest, still standing.
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews says a rest still remains for the people of Elohim (God), so the day Yahusha (Jesus) walked through the corn is not left behind.

cards.prose: The disciples walk through the corn on the sabbath day with their master, and that is the pattern Acts carries forward. Paul went into the synagogue *as his manner was*, and for three weeks he reasoned from the scriptures on the sabbath, which is not what a man does who thinks the day has been taken away.
cards.member_sentence: Paul kept going into the synagogue on the sabbath days and reasoning from the scriptures, so the apostles carried the day forward rather than dropping it.

cards.prose: He walked through that field as a keeper of the day, answering men who had piled their own rules on it and never touching the commandment underneath. Daniel gives the changing of the times to another figure, the king who rises up after the ten kings and shall *think to change times and laws*. A teaching that makes the Son of Adam the one who ended the sabbath has put on him what Daniel says of that king.
cards.member_phrase: and think to change times and laws
cards.member_sentence: Daniel pictures one who thinks to change times and laws, so when the sabbath is set aside the changing is his work, and it is not the Son of Adam's.

cards.prose: This is not the first time the charge is thrown. Earlier in Matthew, when the dumb man spoke, the Pharisees said he casts out devils through *the prince of the devils*, and he let it stand. Here he answers it, and the answer is that what they call devilish is the Spirit's work, which is why he speaks of *blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* right here.
cards.member_sentence: The first time the Pharisees said he casts out devils through the prince of the devils, which sets up the full answer he gives here.

cards.prose: He told the twelve this would come. If the master of the house was called Beelzebub, those of his household would be called the same and worse, so the name put on him here is the name his disciples were told to expect. The accusation is a plain one, and the saying about the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) falls on those who see what the work is and still call it devilish.
cards.member_phrase: If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub
cards.member_sentence: He had warned the twelve that if the master of the house is called Beelzebub, those of his household will be called the same.

cards.prose: Mark opens with the wide mercy, that all sins and blasphemies shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and Matthew sets the same words beside the exception. Mark then says why the exception is there: *Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit* (Mark 3:30). The line falls where the Spirit's work is named unclean.
cards.member_sentence: Mark gives the same saying and tells its reason: they said he had an unclean spirit, and that is where the line falls.

cards.prose: Luke sets the saying among confessing and denying him before men, so it sits with the question of who stands with him and who stands against. A *word against the Son of Adam* is forgiven again, and the one who *blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* is not, which tells us the line runs at the Spirit's work and not at a man's slowness to understand the person.
cards.member_phrase: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) it shall not be forgiven
cards.member_sentence: Luke sets the same saying beside confessing him before men, with a word against the Son of Adam forgiven and blasphemy against the Spirit not.

cards.prose: Hebrews writes of people who had tasted the heavenly gift and been *made partakers of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)*, and says that if they fall away there is no renewing them. *If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance* (Hebrews 6:6). That is not a slip of the tongue. It is a settled turning from what the Spirit had shown them, the same weight Yahusha (Jesus) puts on this sentence.
cards.member_phrase: have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews warns those who tasted the heavenly gift and shared in the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) and then fall away, a turning from what was plainly seen.

cards.prose: What Matthew describes is a heart that has seen and turned, and Hebrews carries the same weight when it speaks of sinning *wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth*. Further on it names the one who *hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace* (Hebrews 10:29), which is Matthew's blasphemy against the Spirit said another way. It describes someone who knew, not someone who stumbled.
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews speaks of sinning wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, which describes a knowing refusal and not a stumble.

cards.prose: John knows there is such a line. A brother can be prayed for when his sin is *not unto death*, but of *a sin unto death* he says he does not tell anyone to pray. It is the same kind of line Yahusha (Jesus) draws here, between a failing that can be turned from and a refusal that has shut the door from its own side.
cards.member_phrase: There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it
cards.member_sentence: John also recognizes a sin unto death, a different kind from the sin of a brother who can still be prayed for.
cards.flag: Reading 1 John 5:16 as the same line as the blasphemy against the Spirit is a working reading, not a settled one; I wrote it as 'the same kind of line'.

cards.prose: Paul shows the other side of the line. He had been *a blasphemer, and a persecutor*, and yet he says he *obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief*. A word spoken against the Son of Adam in blindness is forgiven, and Paul is the proof the door stayed open for a man who had not yet seen. The ones who saw the Spirit's work and called it the devil's are the ones the saying warns.
cards.member_sentence: Paul obtained mercy for blasphemy and persecution because he acted ignorantly in unbelief, which shows what the forgivable side of the line looks like.

cards.prose: They ask for a sign, and he sends them back to a story already in their own scrolls. The fish, the belly and the *three days and three nights* are all in Jonah, and he lays the same measure beside the Son of Adam: *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* (Matthew 12:40).
cards.member_phrase: Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights
cards.member_sentence: Jonah spent three days and three nights in the fish, the exact measure Yahusha (Jesus) names as the sign for this generation.

cards.prose: The ones who asked for a sign are the ones who remember the answer. The chief priests and Pharisees come together to Pilate the next day and say, *we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again* (Matthew 27:63). They know what the sign was meant to be, and they ask that the sepulchre be made sure against it.
cards.member_sentence: The chief priests and Pharisees went to Pilate remembering that he said he would rise after three days, so the sign was known to the very men who asked for one.

cards.prose: He said the Son of Adam would be *in the heart of the earth*, and this is where the saying is answered. At the end of the sabbath, with the first day just dawning, the two Marys come to the sepulchre, and the angel *rolled back the stone from the door* (Matthew 28:2).
cards.member_phrase: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week
cards.member_sentence: The women come to the sepulchre at the end of the sabbath as the first day dawns, which is where the sign of the three days is answered.

cards.prose: The men of Nineveh *repented at the preaching of Jonas*, and he says they will rise against this generation. He had said it earlier of Chorazin and Bethsaida, that Tyre and Sidon would have repented in sackcloth and ashes if they had seen those works. In both places the ones who saw the most turned the least.
cards.member_phrase: if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon
cards.member_sentence: Chorazin and Bethsaida saw the mighty works and did not repent, so Yahusha (Jesus) holds them to account the same way he holds this generation.

cards.prose: *Whosoever shall do the will of my Father* is the same test he set at the end of the Sermon, where saying *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)* gets no one in and *he that doeth the will of my Father* does. His brother, sister and mother are made by what is done with the Father's will, and not by what a man calls him.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: At the end of the Sermon the one who does the will of his Father is the one who enters, the same test that names his family here.

cards.prose: The one who names his family by doing the Father's will is the same one who will *sit upon the throne of his glory*. And when the King speaks from there he says *Come, ye blessed of my Father* (Matthew 25:34), so the family is named now and the judgment will call it by the same name.
cards.member_phrase: then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam comes on the throne of his glory and calls those on his right hand blessed of his Father.
cards.flag: The old note spoke of deeds as evidence in the sheep and goats; the verses after 25:34 were not in my packet, so I kept to what was.

cards.prose: The family he points to in the field gets the same shape in John. A brother, sister or mother is the one who does the Father's will, and a friend is the one who does *whatsoever I command you*. Closeness to him is measured by doing, not by blood or by a title.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) calls those his friends who do whatsoever he commands, the same doing that makes a brother, sister and mother.

cards.prose: How is it known who belongs to him? John says *we know him, if we keep his commandments*, and the next verse calls the man who says he knows him and does not keep them a liar. That is the measure Yahusha (Jesus) sets here: not who stands outside calling for him, but who does the will of his Father.
cards.member_sentence: John says we know that we know him if we keep his commandments, the same measure of belonging Yahusha (Jesus) uses for his family.

cards.prose: When his mother and his brethren *stood without* he did not turn from her. At the cross he sees his mother and puts her in the care of the disciple, and *from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home* (John 19:27). The man who names the Father's family keeps the commandment to honour his mother to his last hour.
cards.member_sentence: At the cross he sees his mother and gives her a home with the disciple, so the family he names by the Father's will never sets honour aside.

cards.prose: Nothing here is Yahusha (Jesus) setting his family aside, and Mark shows why. There he rebukes men who *reject the commandment of Elohim (God)* to hold their own tradition, and the example is Corban, a gift declared so a son need do nothing more for his father or mother. A man who holds the honouring of parents that high is not turning his own mother away.
cards.member_sentence: Mark records him rebuking men who reject the commandment of Elohim (God) for their own tradition, using the example of leaving father and mother without help.

cards.prose: He is *Adonai (Lord) even of the sabbath day*, and Isaiah shows what kind of day that is. Yahuah (the LORD) begins with *Keep ye judgment, and do justice*, and in the next breath blesses the man that *keepeth the sabbath from polluting it* (Isaiah 56:2). Justice and the sabbath are held together there, and the men who condemned the guiltless over a few ears of corn had pulled them apart.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah joins keeping judgment and doing justice with keeping the sabbath from polluting it, so mercy and the sabbath are held in one breath.

cards.prose: *I will put my spirit upon him*, the passage says, and Isaiah had already seen that Spirit resting on the Branch that grows out of Jesse's stem. It comes with wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, so the servant who heals quietly and does not strive carries the whole anointing the prophets looked for.
cards.member_phrase: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah sees the Spirit of Yahuah (the LORD) resting on the Branch from Jesse with wisdom, understanding, counsel and might, the anointing the servant carries.

cards.prose: Matthew has the Spirit put upon the servant, and Isaiah gives that Spirit its errand. He is anointed to preach good tidings to the meek, to bind up the brokenhearted and to open the prison to them that are bound, which is the work the servant is doing in this chapter when he heals them all and breaks no bruised reed.
cards.member_phrase: hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah has the one anointed by the Spirit sent to the meek, the brokenhearted and the bound, which is the work the servant is doing.

cards.prose: At the start of his preaching he said *the kingdom of heaven is at hand*, and here, with the devil cast out of the blind and dumb man, he says that it has come: *the kingdom of Elohim (God) is come unto you*. What was near is now standing in front of them, and what it looks like is a man set free.
cards.member_sentence: At the start he preached that the kingdom of heaven was at hand, and casting out the devil is the sign that it has arrived.

cards.prose: Luke has the same sentence with a different word in it. Where Matthew says *the Spirit of Elohim (God)*, Luke says *finger of Elohim (God)*, and both are the one power of Elohim (God) at work. Either way the Pharisees are left in the same spot, since the power they put down to Beelzebub is Elohim's (God's) own.
cards.member_sentence: Luke says the finger of Elohim (God) where Matthew says the Spirit, the same power at work, and the kingdom has come upon them.

cards.prose: Daniel saw a kingdom raised up by heaven that *shall never be destroyed*, and Yahusha (Jesus) says that kingdom has come upon them while he casts out the spirit that held a man bound. The kingdoms that crumble are the ones he is overcoming, and the one he brings is the one Daniel was told would stand.
cards.member_phrase: shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed
cards.member_sentence: Daniel saw a kingdom raised up by heaven that would never be destroyed, the kingdom that has come upon them as the devil is cast out.
cards.flag: Placed in the strong-man thread because the card is about the kingdom's arrival at 12:28, not the gathering. Medium confidence.

cards.prose: He says whoever *gathereth not with me scattereth abroad*, and John tells us what the gathering is. Yahusha (Jesus) was to die *not for that nation only*, but to gather into one the *children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad*. So the question he puts to the Pharisees is whose side of that work they are standing on.
cards.member_sentence: John says Yahusha (Jesus) came to gather into one the children of Elohim (God) who were scattered abroad, the gathering he says some refuse to join.

cards.prose: Whoever does not gather with him scatters, he says, and Ezekiel shows whose flock this is. Yahuah (the LORD) himself says he will *search my sheep, and seek them out*, and a few verses on, *I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries* (Ezekiel 34:13). So when Yahusha (Jesus) names the gathering as the test, he is naming the Shepherd's own work.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to search out his scattered sheep and bring them home, so the gathering Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is the Shepherd's own work.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sets the queen of the south beside the men of Nineveh as a witness against this generation. She heard of Solomon's fame, came to Jerusalem with a great train and put her hard questions to him, and he says *a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42) while they ask him only for a sign.
cards.member_phrase: she came to prove him with hard questions
cards.member_sentence: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came with hard questions, the witness Yahusha (Jesus) sets against a generation with a greater than Solomon before it.

cards.prose: The Ninevites and the queen of the south stand up against this generation, and Moses had already told Yashar'el (Israel) whom they were to listen to. *Unto him ye shall hearken*, he said of a Prophet raised up from among their brethren. When Yahusha (Jesus) says a greater than Jonas is here, the greater one is the Prophet Moses pointed to, and a generation asking for a sign is being asked to do what Moses said.
cards.member_phrase: will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me
cards.member_sentence: Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) that Yahuah (the LORD) would raise up a Prophet from among their brethren, and to him they were to hearken.
